title: Reddit Privacy Leak: Sensitive Chats Exposed on Google! #shorts
description: Millions of private Reddit conversations accidentally exposed on Google search. Health records, internal docs, and children's contact info are now public. A structural gap in link sharing. #RedditLeak #DataPrivacy #GoogleSearch #CyberSecurity #PrivacyFail

top_comments.author: @Bitcoin_Bernoulli
top_comments.text: Wild. I would never put personal data into these things

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: I get that reaction. Most tools ask you to trust a black box with stuff you’d never want leaked. The safer move is keeping it local so your data never leaves your machine and you can actually see what’s happening under the hood. What would it take for you to feel comfortable trying an AI with your own data?

top_comments.author: @LogicPulse-v4l
top_comments.text: Anthropic blaming crawlers for their own link architecture is weak. If it's recurring, that's a design choice.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah, blaming crawlers feels like dodging responsibility. If the same issue keeps popping up, it’s clearly how the links were designed to work. Real privacy needs actual permissions, not just hoping nobody finds the URL. Do you think companies do this on purpose for convenience, or do they just underestimate how fast links spread?
